name: Blackwell School National Historic Site
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Blackwell School National Historic Site in Marfa, Texas, was established on November 11, 2022, as the 423rd unit of the National Park System. The school operated from the 1880s through 1965 as the segregated school for Mexican American children in the Marfa Independent School District during the era of "Juan Crow" discrimination in Texas. Students were punished for speaking Spanish and faced systematic educational inequality. The site was championed by former students and their descendants — known as the Blackwell School Alliance — who preserved the remaining adobe classroom building and shared their oral histories to ensure this chapter of civil rights history would not be forgotten.
